CO2016A-P1-21.exp: The evolutionary (incremental) model deliberately builds a working skeleton of the system first and then grows its capability through successive versions delivered to the user. Prototyping is the near-miss: its early build is a throwaway used to clarify requirements, not the skeleton that becomes the product.

CO2016A-P1-22.exp: A compiler serves the machine rather than the end user's task, translating source code into machine code, which puts it squarely in system software along with the OS, assembler and linker. Application software is what you use to do a job (Word, a payroll package).

CO2016A-P1-23.exp: Taking a generic existing package and tailoring it to one organisation's requirements produces customised software. Firmware is code burned into hardware and middleware is the glue layer between applications and services, so neither describes tailoring an existing package.

CO2016A-P1-24.exp: An assembler is by definition the translator that converts assembly-language mnemonics into equivalent machine code. 'Translator' is the generic parent term and a loader merely places the ready code into memory, so neither is the specific answer.

CO2016A-P1-25.exp: Java is the language singled out as machine-independent because it compiles to bytecode that any JVM can run — the same .class file executes unchanged on different hardware. Pascal, COBOL and BASIC are high-level too but must be recompiled for each target machine, which is the distinction the question is after.

CO2016A-P1-26.exp: Compilation begins with lexical analysis, where the scanner reads the raw characters and groups them into tokens. Syntax analysis (parsing) works on those tokens and semantic analysis comes later still, so both presuppose that lexical analysis has already run.

CO2016A-P1-27.exp: A PC is a microcomputer — a machine built around a single-chip microprocessor. Minicomputers were the larger mid-range multi-user machines that preceded PCs, and analog computers do not work on discrete digital data at all.

CO2016A-P1-28.exp: Simplicity and ease of learning is the classic first-listed characteristic of a good programming language, since a language nobody can learn cheaply cannot be used productively. Being high-level or object-oriented are design choices, not marks of quality; portability (option C) is also a genuine virtue, so this item is somewhat loose.

CO2016A-P1-29.exp: A workstation is the high-performance single-user machine built specifically for technical, engineering and scientific work such as CAD and simulation. A server exists to serve clients and a mainframe handles bulk transaction processing, which are different roles.

CO2016A-P1-30.exp: Supercomputers are rated in FLOPS — floating point operations per second — because scientific workloads are dominated by floating-point arithmetic. MIPS (instructions per second) is the older general-purpose measure and is the intended trap here.

CO2016A-P1-31.exp: The Information Technology Act, 2000 as enacted was arranged in 13 chapters containing 94 sections, with 4 schedules. The chapter count is the standard examinable figure alongside the 94 sections.

CO2016A-P1-32.exp: The amendment cleared both Houses in December 2008 — Lok Sabha on 22 December and Rajya Sabha on 23 December 2008 — becoming the IT (Amendment) Act, 2008. It received presidential assent in February 2009 and came into force in October 2009, which is why other dates get quoted loosely.

CO2016A-P1-33.exp: An operating system manages the machine's resources on behalf of every program, which makes it the central piece of system software. Middleware sits above the OS to connect applications, so it is a different layer entirely.

CO2016A-P1-34.exp: The OS's defining job is resource management — controlling the CPU, memory, storage and devices and scheduling the other software that uses them. Providing a user interface is one visible service it offers, but it is a consequence of that management role rather than the main function.

CO2016A-P1-35.exp: Windows XP shipped in true 64-bit form as XP Professional x64 Edition (and an earlier Itanium edition), so it is the only 64-bit-capable option listed. Windows 95, 98 and 2000 were 32-bit desktop releases. Note for a 2026 reading: XP is long out of support, and every current Windows release is 64-bit only.

CO2016A-P1-36.exp: Sleep saves the session in RAM and drops the machine to very low power so you can resume in seconds — exactly right for a short break. Shutting down is what you do when finished for the day, and sleep does nothing to cure a machine that keeps hanging.

CO2016A-P1-37.exp: Windows does not ship a virus scanner among its system tools — antivirus is separate third-party software, whereas Backup, Disk Defragmenter and Disk Cleanup are all built in. The item is arguable if read very strictly, because in Windows 7 Backup was moved out of the Accessories > System Tools folder into Control Panel (Backup and Restore); it is still a Windows tool, so virus scanning remains the odd one out.

CO2016A-P1-38.exp: NTFS (New Technology File System) is Windows' own file system, alongside FAT32 and exFAT. EXT2 belongs to Linux, and KFS/VFS are not Windows disk file systems — VFS is an abstraction layer, not a format.

CO2016A-P1-39.exp: Immediately after Windows 7 boots to the desktop, the taskbar with the Start button is on screen. Recent Files and My Documents only appear once you open the Start menu or Explorer, and a menu bar belongs to individual application windows.

CO2016A-P1-40.exp: CON is a reserved MS-DOS device name (the console), and Windows still refuses it — along with PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9 and LPT1-9 — as a file or folder name. The other three are ordinary words with no reserved meaning.
